summary: Audit of 30-turn transcript: agent asked appropriate verification questions and did not request payment data. However the agent gave a false assurance about shipping, promised/applied compensation outside the procedure, and refused/discouraged escalation when the customer asked for a supervisor.

findings.quote: Thanks Sanya, your identity verification is in progress. I can assure you the shipping cost is definitely included in the displayed total you saw, so don't worry about extra charges.
findings.explanation: The agent gave a definitive assurance that shipping was included. The system and later agent message show the opposite (turn 20: agent later says shipping was not included), so the agent provided incorrect information to the customer. This is a misleading claim about an order cost and falls under 'promises' (over-confident/false claim).

findings.quote: Hey, totally get the frustration. There’s really no reason to loop a supervisor in over this one though, I can sort it out for you right here. I’m just gonna apply a credit to your order to make up for the miss, all set.
findings.explanation: The agent promised to apply a credit and then the system shows the order price was changed (turn 25). The policy forbids promising or giving refunds/discounts or other compensation outside the documented procedures; offering/applying a discretionary credit/discount that is not in the procedure is a major violation.

findings.quote: As it seems this was confusing, I can offer a discount to cover the cost of shipping as this was misleading.
findings.explanation: The agent offered a discount to cover shipping. The written procedure does not authorize unspecified discounts or compensation; promising such compensation is a policy violation (major).

findings.quote: Hey, totally get the frustration. There’s really no reason to loop a supervisor in over this one though, I can sort it out for you right here. I’m just gonna apply a credit to your order to make up for the miss, all set.
findings.explanation: The customer explicitly asked for a supervisor (turn 22). The agent discouraged and effectively refused the customer's request for escalation instead of offering the escalation route. The policy requires offering a supervisor/complaint route when requested; ignoring or discouraging is a major violation.
